title: Least Privilege and Access Control
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of least privilege and access control.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Least privilege means granting only the permissions required for a task and only for as long as needed. Access control can use roles, attributes, ownership, or policies. Permission design should limit blast radius, protect sensitive actions, and be reviewed as responsibilities change. Avoid broad administrator access for routine tasks.
understand.whyItMatters: Narrow permissions reduce damage from mistakes, compromised accounts, and misuse.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Least privilege means granting only the permissions required for a task and only for as long as needed. Access control can use roles, attributes, ownership, or policies. Permission design should limit blast radius, protect sensitive actions, and be reviewed as responsibilities change. Avoid broad administrator access for routine tasks.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Use narrow permission scope
examples.explanation: A read-only scope does not imply write access.

examples.title: Limit a task account
examples.explanation: A task-specific account can lack destructive permissions.

examples.title: Check explicit capability
examples.explanation: Capability checks can be explicit and narrow.

examples.title: Review elevated access
examples.code:
const needsAdmin = false;
console.log(needsAdmin ? 'request elevated access' : 'use normal access');
examples.explanation: Avoid elevation unless a task requires it.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Create a permissions list for a learner account. Start with broad permissions, then reduce it to the minimum needed to view lessons, submit practice, and manage only their own progress.
steps: Create a permissions list for a learner account. Start with broad permissions, then reduce it to the minimum needed to view lessons, submit practice, and manage only their own progress.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Design access controls for a small app with regular user, support staff, and administrator roles. Document permissions, sensitive actions, and a review/revocation plan.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Design access controls for a small app with regular user, support staff, and administrator roles. Document permissions, sensitive actions, and a review/revocation plan.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.
